headline: Giuliani got his medal. Trump promised it in 2025.
summary: Trump gave Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor, on Tuesday. Giuliani, 82, led New York after the Sept. 11 attacks. As Trump's lawyer he made election claims courts rejected, lost a $148 million defamation case to two Georgia election workers, and was disbarred in New York and Washington.

cover_question.q: What did he do to get a medal?

cover_answer: He led New York City after the 9/11 attacks.
table_question: Should a prize count the whole person or their best day?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president gave a man named Rudy Giuliani a medal, the biggest one a person who isn't a soldier can get. He was the mayor of New York City 25 years ago, when the city was attacked, and he helped it get through. A medal like this is like a gold star, but from the president. Nothing changes for you.
5-7.why: A gold star from the president. That is the whole thing at seven.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, and a medal is a thing they know: a gold star, a sticker, a ribbon at sports day. The script gives them that and one job he did, helping a city after an attack, and stops. Expect 'can I get one?' Not this one. Then ask what they would give a medal for, and listen.

8-12.script: The Medal of Freedom is the top honor a president gives. Trump gave it Tuesday to Rudy Giuliani, New York's mayor during the Sept. 11 attacks. Since then he was Trump's lawyer, courts threw out his 2020 election claims, and he lost his law license. Like a teacher's award: the giver decides.
8-12.why: Mayor, lawyer, license gone, medal. The order is the argument.
8-12.why_long: At 10 a child is testing whether adults apply rules consistently, and here the rule is what a medal is for. The script hands them the order: mayor in 2001, Trump's lawyer, claims thrown out, license gone, medal. The teacher's award is the mechanism: the giver decides. Expect 'can he be a lawyer again?' Not in New York or Washington.

13-17.script: Does one great chapter earn a lifetime medal? Giuliani led New York after Sept. 11. As Trump's lawyer he made election claims courts rejected, lost $148 million to two Georgia election workers, and was disbarred. Second: Tiger Woods and Elvis Presley have this medal too. Who decides what it means?
13-17.why: Two true things: the 2001 mayor and the disbarred lawyer are one man.
13-17.why_long: At 14 they can hold two true things at once: the mayor who led New York through Sept. 11 and the lawyer disbarred for false election claims are one man. The script asks whether a medal weighs a life or a chapter, then widens it to Tiger Woods and Elvis Presley. Expect 'can a president give it to anyone?' The article names no rule.

5-7.a: For doing something a lot of people think was brave or important. This one is for helping New York after it was attacked.

8-12.q: What did he do to get a medal?
8-12.a: Mayor of New York during the Sept. 11 attacks. He led the city after.

8-12.q: Why do some people think he shouldn't get it?
8-12.a: He said 2020 was stolen. Courts said no. He lost his law license.

13-17.q: Isn't it odd to honor someone who was disbarred?
13-17.a: Plenty think so. Trump calls him New York's greatest mayor.

13-17.q: Who else has Trump given it to?
13-17.a: Tiger Woods, Rush Limbaugh and Mariano Rivera, among others.
